findings.title: timezone.now() default is evaluated once at class definition time
findings.body: The default value `queued: datetime = timezone.now()` is evaluated once when the module is first imported, not at each instance creation. All `AssignmentSource` instances created without an explicit `queued` argument will share the same timestamp (the time the module was loaded). This is a classic Python default-argument pitfall. The fix is to use `field(default_factory=timezone.now)` from `dataclasses`. While `queued` is not currently used in any logic, this produces misleading data and will become a real bug if the field is ever used for staleness checks or debugging.

findings.title: datetime object in task kwargs may not be JSON-serializable
findings.body: `assignment_source.to_dict()` (via `dataclasses.asdict`) produces a dict containing a `datetime` object for the `queued` field. This dict is passed as a Celery task kwarg (`assignment_source_dict`). If Celery is configured with JSON serialization (which is Sentry's default), `datetime` objects are not JSON-serializable and the task will fail to enqueue with a `TypeError`. The `queued` field should be converted to an ISO-8601 string in `to_dict()`, or omitted from serialization entirely since it is not used downstream.

findings.title: queued field is never consumed by any logic
findings.body: The `queued` timestamp field is stored and serialized but never read or compared anywhere in this PR or its call sites. If it is intended for future staleness/TTL checks, that logic is missing; if it is purely informational, it adds serialization risk (see the JSON issue) and maintenance burden with no current benefit. Consider removing it or documenting its intended future use.

findings.title: Abstract method sync_status_outbound signature change may break subclasses
findings.body: The `sync_status_outbound` abstract method now includes an explicit `assignment_source` parameter before `**kwargs`. Any concrete subclass that overrides this method with a fixed parameter list (no `**kwargs`) will raise a `TypeError` at call time when the new keyword argument is passed. While the parameter has a default value, callers may begin passing it explicitly. All downstream implementations should be audited to confirm they accept `**kwargs` or have been updated.
